headline: Find the first strict upper bound and wrap around
statement: Given sorted letters with at least two distinct lowercase characters and a target character, return the smallest letter strictly greater than target. If no letter is greater, return the first letter.
constraints: letters is sorted and contains at least two distinct lowercase English letters
target is a lowercase English letter
intuition: All letters <= target lie before all valid answers. Binary search this boundary with a half-open interval. If the boundary is beyond the array, the problem’s circular rule returns index zero.
approach: Search [left,right) for the first letter > target.
Move left past mid when letters[mid] <= target; otherwise lower right to mid.
correctness: The search maintains that all indices below left are <= target and all indices at or above right are > target. Updating by the middle comparison preserves these partitions until left==right is the first valid index. Modulo converts the no-valid-letter boundary to the stipulated wraparound answer.
bruteForce: Scan from the beginning until a letter greater than target is encountered; this costs O(n).

complexity.explanation: Binary search halves the candidate range; wraparound takes constant time.

pitfalls: The comparison is strictly greater; duplicates equal to target must be skipped.
Wrap to the first letter when the insertion point equals len(letters).
